extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, agency staff, Congress, and IP stakeholders (patent and trademark applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the USPTO’s FY2023 performance indicators, customer experience (CX) metrics, training program requirements for patent and trademark examiners, and operational/data/IT modernization standards relevant to patent and trademark administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of prioritized countries progress metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of prioritized countries for which IP country teams have made progress on at least three of the four performance criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This KPI tracks progress on international capacity building and strategic plans for prioritized countries (table shows targets and actuals; FY2023 actual exceeded target).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number trained on IP protection and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of people, including Foreign Government Officials and U.S. Stakeholders trained on best practices to protect and enforce IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts participants in capacity-building and training workshops targeted to audiences like police, prosecutors, customs and border enforcement officials; used as a KPI (FY2023 actuals reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: HISP designated service focus and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: As a High Impact Service Provider (HISP), the USPTO focuses on service assessments, collecting customer feedback, and making measured improvements for two designated services: applying for a patent, and applying to register a trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per OMB Circular A-11 section 280, HISP status requires the agency to maintain CX action plans, assess service performance, and publicly report commitments (e.g., 2023 HISP CX Action Plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer satisfaction with designated priority services (Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of customers who indicate positive satisfaction with designated priority services – Patents: Seeking assistance when filing a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a performance indicator with targets and actuals; methodology changes and target adjustments may occur when CX management platforms or survey models change (e.g., addition of trust question).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee helpfulness metric (Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of customers who indicate the employees they interacted with were helpful – Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via customer surveys; scores inform CX improvements and target adjustments when survey methodology changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust metric for USPTO CX
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of customers who trust USPTO to grant patents and register trademarks in accordance with U.S. laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New measure added following OMB Circular A-11 Section 280 update to include a trust question; used across FY2024–FY2025 planning and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of customer feedback and human-centered design for Patent/Trademark Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance Patent Center and Trademark Center via usability testing of wireframes, prototype testing with customers, feedback collection, analysis of support tickets, and multiple channels for customer feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices include usability testing prior to development, closed beta volunteer participation, surveys, forms, and analyzing support tickets to identify pain points; improvements target navigation, fee transparency, save functionality, and streamlined filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcome letters to applicants to improve CX and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Sending 'welcome letters' to patent and trademark applicants that provide information on free trainings and resources to help navigate the application process and IP ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to bridge gaps (e.g., applicants filing without experienced professionals, lower persistence rates for women sole inventors) by informing recipients of no-cost resources and trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Patent Examiner Training (mandatory two-phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-phase, year-long mandatory training for new patent examiners: a four-month 'residency' in the Office of Patent Training followed by on-the-job just-in-time training in technology centers during the remainder of the first year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers U.S. legal statutes and rules for patent examination, technical subjects, and soft skills; FY2023 metrics: 423,400 hours of patent examination training for 644 new examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for Experienced Examiners (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional training for examiners with one year of experience, designed to keep skills sharp through courses on examination, automation, and soft skills (workload management, stakeholder communication) and internal cross-area learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2023 provided 189 patent examiner topics to 14,985 participants for 26,193 hours; used to maintain and update examiner competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice and Procedures Across Technologies (case law review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing education courses such as 'Case Law Review: Recent Federal Circuit and Supreme Court Decisions' to keep examiners current on legal developments affecting examination practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In FY2023 USPTO provided a cumulative 25,767 hours of this training.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house Patent Law and Evidence Course (mandatory for GS-12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory training for all GS-12 patent examiners covering authoritative court decisions concerning statutory issues under 35 U.S.C. §§101, 102, 103, and 112 and decisions concerning the handling of evidence during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2023: 5,565 hours delivered to 159 participants; explicitly ties examiner competency to core statutory case law and evidence-handling standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examiner Technical Training Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Program enabling examiners to learn from external subject-matter experts (scientists, engineers, designers, industry and academic experts) about technological advances, emerging trends, and recent innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivered virtually to allow broad participation; FY2023 hosted 104 events with 31,502 participants for 44,957 hours (average 5.49 hours per examiner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Site Experience Education (SEE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program providing technology education 'at its source' via coordinated site visits so examiners can see current and emerging technologies firsthand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2023: 19 SEE trips with 242 participants visiting 80 commercial, industrial, and academic sites across 10 states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspiring Managers Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-month cohort-based developmental program combining assessments, classroom training, workshops, shadowing, and mentoring to develop leadership, interpersonal, and technical skills for Patents organization managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporates all 10 USPTO Leader Profile Qualities; used for succession into supervisory patent examiner and trainer roles; FY2023 delivered 1,833 hours to 30 participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-duty Hours Legal and Technical Studies Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs that reimburse eligible employees for mission-related legal (JD) or technical coursework at accredited institutions to broaden legal or technical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-duty Hours Legal Studies reimbursed 100% tuition for 93 participants (FY2023); Non-duty Technical Training had 24 active participants; participation is mission-related and subject to eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Administrative Continued Education (PACE) and Upward Mobility Program (UMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: PACE provides a dynamic curriculum focused on employee engagement and adult learning; UMP is the largest component focused on career development for positions with limited advancement, aiding succession planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2023: PACE 28,713 hours to 961 participants; UMP 20,316 hours to 485 participants. Used to enhance professional development across administrative staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Trademark Examining Attorney Training – Trademark Academy
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-phase, nine-month mandatory training for new trademark examining attorneys: a two-month foundational phase followed by law office work with continuing training throughout the academy time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides in-depth introduction to U.S. trademark statutes/rules, technical systems, and soft skills; FY2023 delivered 28,900 hours to 85 newly hired trademark examining attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and Classification Training (Trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refresher and introductory training on identification and classification principles, common errors, and guidance on Nice Classification obligations and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Identification and Classification Refresher' for experienced examiners and 'Intro to ID/Class' for Trademark Academy offices; FY2023 sessions reached 125+ examiners and >500 participants for Nice 12-2023 updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining Attorney Training and TM Refresh
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing trademark examining attorney training addressing new systems (TM Exam, X-Search) and refresher modules (TM Refresh) informed by quality review data to target decided areas needing training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined training resulted in 6,141 hours in FY2023; the USPTO seeks to incorporate continuing legal education credits where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Law Library and Service Units Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Webcast training on evidence-gathering resources, research skills, configuration/design searching, plus unit-specific training (Pre-Exam, Legal Instruments, Intent to Use, Madrid Processing, Post Registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law library delivered group and individual trainings and 'flash trainings'; Service Units training provides new employee and ongoing business-unit-specific education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and Supervisor Development in Trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs like TM Talks Supervisor Training and Leadership Journey Series to provide on-the-job training, leadership stories, and sessions tailored to supervisors and aspiring leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include merit system principles, labor relations, virtual employee management, project management, and career insights; delivered live and recorded to reach broad audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' annual performance agreements and bonus criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual performance agreements between Commissioners (Patents and Trademarks) and the Secretary of Commerce that outline measurable organizational goals and objectives used to evaluate performance and determine bonuses (up to 50% of base salary, subject to aggregate limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements define evaluation criteria and measurable organizational goals; bonus awards depend on performance evaluations specified in the agreements; bonus data reported in APPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance data verification and validation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO requirement for complete, accurate, and reliable performance data to assess progress toward strategic objectives and to support management decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency conducts verification/validation processes for KPI data reported in performance tables; reliability of these data is foundational to APPR reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data as an Enterprise Asset (DaaEA) initiative standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish principles, processes, and procedures that enable a transparent data and analytics culture, including formation of a Data and Analytics Council, enterprise data maturity assessment, data strategy and roadmap, and inventory/catalog of USPTO data assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Near-term plans include building a data governance operating model with well-defined roles/responsibilities, literacy plans and skills assessments, and creating a data asset catalog to improve discovery, accountability, and use across the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT modernization and cloud adoption practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Move critical systems to a modern data center and public cloud providers to enhance disaster recovery, resilience, and enable scalable deployment; regularly simulate outages and failovers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cloud Smart Services provide consulting, testing environment support, and co-prototyping; cybersecurity authorizations obtained for AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform; migration decisions guided by business sense and security.
